name: The Nuclear Century: Fear, Power and the Bomb
description: From the first chain reaction to the bomb, the reactor, the arms race and the accidents that followed: how splitting the atom shaped the world after 1939.

checkpoints.name: The race for the bomb
checkpoints.note: Szilard and Einstein warned of a chain reaction in 1939. Fermi's pile in Chicago proved it in 1942, and the Manhattan Project, with Oppenheimer directing the Los Alamos laboratory and Hans Bethe leading its theorists, built the weapons tested at Trinity and used on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

checkpoints.name: Fear and promise
checkpoints.note: The Atomic Age and the Cold War brought hydrogen bombs, missiles that could cross oceans, standoffs such as the Cuban Missile Crisis, and in 1968 a treaty to limit the spread of weapons. Nuclear reactors fed a grid at Obninsk and drove the submarine Nautilus, and Godzilla gave the fear a monster's face.

checkpoints.name: Accidents and fusion dreams
checkpoints.note: Three Mile Island, Chernobyl and Fukushima shook trust in nuclear power and left zones where people cannot live. Meanwhile tokamaks and ITER pursue fusion, the cleaner power of the stars.
